sections.html:
Two offices share the job. Your town, or the City of Eagle River, takes the first installment. The Vilas County Treasurer takes the second installment plus every late payment. The treasurer is at 330 Court Street, Eagle River, WI 54521, with weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, phone 715-479-3609.

By law that office receives county money, keeps the books, collects postponed and delinquent real estate tax and reconciles with local municipalities. Visitors pass through lobby security first. At the window you can hand over cash, a check, a money order, a cashier's check or a card.

Ownership and parcel descriptions live with the Real Property Listing office in the Land Information Department: (715) 479-3696 or rpl@vilascountywi.gov. Its online tools include a tax lookup in the Ascent Land Records Suite with bills from 2020 forward, an older lookup for 2011 through 2022 bills, and an opt-out form for owners who want their name hidden from searches.

Pay the whole bill or the first half at your local treasurer by January 31. The second half goes to the county by July 31. Wis. Stat. 74.11 divides the tax into two equal halves; a bill below $100 must be paid in one piece by January 31.

If a half is still not in hand five working days after its due date, everything unpaid turns delinquent: February 1 for the first half, August 1 for the second. Overdue money goes to the county treasurer, which means a missed January payment is settled in Eagle River. The county starts taking second installments on February 1.

Delinquent real estate tax accrues 1% interest per month or fraction of one, and the county board can layer on a penalty of up to 0.5% monthly (Wis. Stat. 74.47). The treasurer can tell you which charges the county applies and give a payoff for your closing day.

Options include the counter, the mail, a website and a phone line, each with timing limits. Point and Pay processes the web and phone payments, and only for second installments and delinquent taxes. It adds 2.39% on cards and $1.50 on an electronic check. The phone line, 1-866-518-2304, shuts down from December 1 through January 31.

  • Mail: payee is Vilas County Treasurer, the parcel number goes on the check, and a stamped return envelope gets you a receipt.
  • Near a deadline: hand the envelope to a post office clerk and request a hand postmark. Checks sent by a bank's bill-pay service often show no postmark, and the bank's confirmation proves nothing about timeliness.
  • Counter: carry the parcel number or the coupon from the bill so staff credit the right property.

Report address changes before November 15, ahead of the December mailing. Senior owners should also watch for a property tax scam that the state has publicized.

Every town, plus the City of Eagle River, hires a private assessment firm, and the Real Property Listing office keeps the roster.

Phone numbers for each firm are on the Real Property Listing page.

If the value looks wrong, take it to the local board of review. Its 45-day window opens on the fourth Monday of April, and you must alert the clerk at least 48 hours before objecting (Wis. Stat. 70.47). Expect the board to presume the assessor is right. Recent sales or an appraisal are your best evidence.

Owners who occupy the house as a primary residence on January 1 may get the Wisconsin lottery and gaming credit off the bill. It is not available on rentals, vacant land or garages. If your bill omits it, apply at the municipal treasurer's office by January 31, or file late with the Department of Revenue by October 1.

A cabin or second home is ineligible. At a sale the credit stays attached to the parcel, so include it when you prorate, and an occupying buyer submits a new application.

sections.h2: What happens when taxes are not paid?
sections.html:
Vilas County goes after delinquent property through an in rem tax foreclosure, carried out by the county treasurer. If you owe, the balance can usually be paid out of closing proceeds, and Wis. Stat. 74.51 lets anyone discharge delinquent real property taxes, with interest and any penalty, before a tax certificate issues.

Wis. Stat. 74.49 allows partial payments of $20 or more on delinquent taxes. Late payments are accepted year-round, so you can bring an account current whenever you like. Request a written payoff valid through your closing date.

Vilas is northern lake country whose market runs on tourism and second homes. Population is 23,761 (2025 estimate), up 3.1% since April 2020, with 37.1% of residents 65 or older. Median home value among owners is $300,000, and 84.0% of housing units are owner-occupied. Households number 11,147 against 25,498 housing units, which points to seasonal use.

Lake cottages often sell on a different schedule than town houses. A winter closing can complicate access and inspections, and the July installment still comes due, so discuss all three with your agent or buyer.

sections.h2: What to ask before you list
sections.html:
Get the parcel's tax history, and any delinquency, from the treasurer. Have the Real Property Listing office confirm the name and mailing address on the parcel. Renting to vacationers? The county website carries a Tourist Rooming Houses page under its Business menu, and the county can tell you what approval, if any, passes to a buyer. Check before promising that the rental income transfers.

Gather what the title company will ask for: the newest bill, proof of payments and, if money is owed, a written payoff. With a cash buyer no lender reviews these items, yet title work still verifies them before closing.

A workable order of operations: confirm the January payment went to the right local treasurer, pull the bill history from the lookup tool, ask the county treasurer for a payoff if anything is delinquent, and hand all of it to the closing agent. If the second installment is not yet due when you close, expect it to be prorated between you and the buyer. Keep your parcel number on every request, since both county offices search by it.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my first installment in Vilas County?
faqs.a: Locally: the town treasurer, or the City of Eagle River. On-time first-half and full payments are made there, while the county takes July money and late payments.

faqs.q: What is the Vilas County Treasurer's address and phone?
faqs.a: The office sits at 330 Court Street, Eagle River, WI 54521, and answers at 715-479-3609. It is open weekdays 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM; holiday closings appear on the county website.

faqs.q: Can I pay Vilas County taxes online?
faqs.a: Yes, for second installments and delinquent taxes, through Point and Pay. Cards cost 2.39% and electronic checks cost $1.50. First installments go to your local municipality, which can say whether it offers an online option.

faqs.q: How is the Vilas County foreclosure process different?
faqs.a: The county uses an in rem tax foreclosure, run by the county treasurer. An owner in arrears can discharge the taxes with interest before a tax certificate issues.

faqs.q: Does the lottery credit carry to the buyer of a Vilas County home?
faqs.a: Yes, it stays with the parcel and belongs in the proration. A buyer who moves in as a primary resident files a fresh application.
